title: And Then The Rodeo Burned Down by Xhloe and Natasha at Ars Nova #xhlo...
transcript: What exactly IS a rodeo clown? It sounds like a thankless role that would be held by a nobody, akin to a court jester, but Xhloe and Natasha have used it as a springboard to meditate on labor, capitalism, and social hierarchy. Through their signature movement and precise choreography, they tell the story of Dale, a rodeo clown who longs to become a cowboy someday. He's accompanied by an enigmatic sidekick who self-describes as his shadow and adds a more interpretive and psychological lens to the show. The plot is initially pretty simple, but things unravel quickly — they take us in a lot of directions in just 70 minutes. Much like the other pieces I've seen by Xhloe and Natasha, it's full of whimsy and humor while packing plenty of unexpected moments of poignance and melancholy. The way the two of them navigate the movement and the emotional beats in perfect synchronicity is marvelous and worth the price of admission in itself, but I was also delighted to see them have a bigger production value. The space is completely decked out to align with the show, making it more immersive without stifling the intimacy of the performance. And Then The Rodeo Burned Down is running at the Ars Nova only through July 2nd, so catch it while you can. With that, another program for my collection.
